issue.title: Resolve decisions:unblocked-tasks-are-offered supersession after successor-card verdicts (record declined, supersede approved)
issue.description:
Decide how `decisions:unblocked-tasks-are-offered` should record that successor-card verdicts (epic bob-cli-hn, plan `plan:202611/successor_card_verdicts.md`) partly retired it.

**What changed in the product.** Every successor card (Obsidian picker, Bob Mac Capture Pull-In card, `bob capture -x/--complete-offer` and `-X/--cancel-offer`) can now resolve an offer row Done or Cancel in the same commit instead of leaving it to recover. A card-resolved row is closed root-only. Its dependents recover with `[unblocked:: today]` under the WRITE rule and are never offered (one offer round per gesture). The contract is `docs/task-dependencies.md` §12.22–§12.23. The record's claim "Unpicked rows recover without a link and resurface through the existing freshness rules." is now incomplete: a row can also be closed in the card, and then it does not resurface.

**Why this is a task and not an edit.** The epic's reviewer decisions conflict. `memory_offers_supersede = yes` authorized marking this record `metadata.status: superseded-in-part` with `superseded_by` naming the new record `decisions:successor-cards-resolve-with-staged-verdicts`, plus a one-line back-link. `memory_verdict_record = no` declined creating that record. The decisions web requires a superseding record and a `superseded_by` target, so the authorized mark cannot be applied. Phases bob-cli-hn.1 (note #1), bob-cli-hn.2 (note #1), and bob-cli-hn.3 (note #4) each flagged this collision, and the bob-cli-hn land agent left memory unchanged.

**Options for Bryan:**
1. Approve the new record `decisions:successor-cards-resolve-with-staged-verdicts`, using the draft in the plan's contract phase, step 5. Then apply the authorized supersede mark and back-link on `decisions:unblocked-tasks-are-offered`.
2. Leave `decisions:unblocked-tasks-are-offered` unmarked and close this task as canceled. The verdict behavior stays documented only in `docs/task-dependencies.md` §12.22.
